item.title: XSide 1.2.0-beta
item.description:
1.1.0 was written but never published as a version of its own: everything it brought is part of 1.2.0, so a user coming from 1.0.6 sees it all here (its What's New shows these items too).

Added

  • The XSide module in the apps: settings per device, kept in step between the Mac and the iPhone. Each installation (app on a device) has its own XSide settings. A change made on the Mac or the iPhone reaches the other side at the next connection; field by field, the most recent change wins (a tie goes to the iPhone). Old state loads as before.
  • An "XSide Settings" page in the app's iOS Settings (touch and hold the app's icon > XSide Settings, or Settings > Apps > [app name] > XSide Settings, behind one row; in English or French, translated by iOS into the app's own languages; XSide adds no language to the app): valid until, last refreshed, version, and the switches below. The footer says that choices apply at once on the device and that XSide on the Mac is told at the next connection.
  • Refresh and pause from the iPhone. XSide answers its apps on the local network (Bonjour _xside._tcp), over a channel signed with a secret per installation, nonces and a time window: refresh now, pause or resume automatic refreshes, and a check-in at each launch (and on return to the app) that reports the app's settings and last refresh and brings the Mac's changes. Turning Automatic refresh off or on in the app's iOS Settings tells XSide at once. iOS asks to allow the local network the first time; macOS may ask to allow incoming connections for XSide (explained in the app). The iPhone waits and retries up to 20 seconds. A refresh asked from the phone is limited in rate, and one the phone didn't hear back about is resolved by the check-in.
  • Live while the app is open: while an app is on screen, it keeps a signed connection open to XSide, and a change made on the Mac (a setting, a pause or resume, from My apps, the panel or xside) is written to it the moment it's stored, so it shows in the app at once, in the usual pill. Every line XSide writes is signed for that app and that connection and numbered, and the app checks each one: nobody else on the network can send it settings or replay an old line. Only an app whose request is signed holds such a connection (one per app, a few per device), XSide renews it every 5 minutes, and the app closes it when it leaves the screen. When it can't be opened (an older XSide, the Mac away), the app checks in every 15 seconds (45 in Low Power Mode) as before. Never before the local network was allowed, and never in the background. On the Mac, the check-in that delivers a change made there is recorded at once, so My apps says it arrived; the Mac's log names the fields each answer changes, and the app logs what it adopted and shows (lines starting with "XSide:").
  • Settings sync feedback in the app, one pill per change that says what changed: settings changed in iOS Settings are sent when the app opens, and one pill says which and that XSide on the Mac knows ("Reminder before expiry" turned off: XSide on your Mac knows), or that the Mac is unreachable and they go at the next connection. A change made on the Mac shows once, the same way ("automatic refresh turned back on from XSide on your Mac"; several are listed under "settings updated from your Mac"), and opens the app's page in iOS Settings; only "None" (every XSide message off) hides it, and turning messages off from the Mac is still said once. At launch, XSide is asked first, so the pill shows things as they are now, and the news replaces the plain validity line.
  • A pill at launch ("XSide: ...") says how many days the app stays valid, then goes away. On by default, per app.
  • A late alert: if XSide couldn't refresh in time (less than the refresh threshold minus 6 hours left), the pill turns orange, then red under a day, with what to do and a Refresh button. When automatic refresh is off for the app, it says so with the expiry date instead.
  • Per app, switches for the card after a refresh, the reminder before expiry (replaces the single global reminder switch), automatic refresh, and the language of XSide's messages (automatic, English, French). On the Mac, a single choice (All, Essentials, None, or Custom) summarizes the four switches.
  • Touch and hold the app's icon: XSide Settings, Refresh now, Report a problem (localized), right from the install. They are written into the app after its own quick actions, in the places those leave (iOS shows 4); an app that sets its quick actions while running shows fewer of its own.
  • "Refresh at next launch" in the app's iOS Settings, now alone at the top of XSide Settings with a footer: it refreshes the app the next time you open it, with nothing to do on your Mac — XSide just needs to be open on your Mac, with this device on the same Wi-Fi or plugged in by USB.
  • Settings > My apps: pick the device (a card with its full name, a menu when there are several), then one of its apps (icon, name, version, days left, a Paused badge) for the same options (the app's ... menu in the panel opens it on that app), applied at the app's next refresh or opening. For each device it says plainly where things stand: "App open on <device>: changes arrive live" (while the app holds its live connection, or, when it polls, until its next check-in is due: 15 seconds, 45 in Low Power Mode, plus a few; it changes by itself shortly after the app leaves the screen), "Changes will arrive the next time the app opens", "Not connected yet: open the app and allow the local network", "Not seen since ..."; what is pending, by name ("Automatic refresh: on — pending"); and "<device> received your settings (on ...)" once it confirmed them. Nothing is claimed active before the iPhone confirmed it.
  • Uninstall or remove an app from Settings > My apps. A ⋯ menu in the page's header carries the panel row's actions (Refresh now, Pause ▸ with the same durations, Stop refreshing or Resume, Remove from the list, Uninstall from <device>), and the bottom of the XSide module tab has Remove from the list and Uninstall from <device> in red. Same confirmations and the same stop refreshing fallback when the device is out of reach; the page is greyed while XSide works on the app, shows a spinner while it uninstalls, and moves to the device's next app once one is gone. The panel's right-click entry now names the app (XSide settings for <app>…).
  • Install without XSide features, for apps that refuse to launch because they detect a change: for all apps (Settings > XSide module in the apps) or per app (step 3, and Settings > My apps), after a confirmation listing what's lost. XSide keeps refreshing them; the per-app choice wins over the default. Applies at each app's next refresh.
  • Pause one app for a while: an app's ... menu in the panel has Pause > For 2 hours, For 1 day or Until I resume (the former Stop refreshing). The row shows "Paused until ..." with the paused look and Resume; the app's own pause ends by itself, and the app on the iPhone is told like any pause from the Mac, with when it resumes.
  • The panel shows who paused an app's refreshes (this iPhone, this iPad or the Mac) and uses two-line subtitles.
  • A My apps tile at the top of the panel, beside Install, Refresh all and Pause, opens Settings > My apps directly.
  • The install window in steps (Devices, Install, XSide module in the app; Tweaks was added between the last two in 1.2.0) with Next/Back and clickable steps; Install at the last one. Settings > Installing > Review the options at each install (on by default): off, an app already installed shows the full list of what will apply, with Edit.
  • Step 3 explains every option with a one-line description and a preview (pill, late alert, card, notification), plus a highlighted box saying where to find the settings later on the iPhone, with the app's name: touch and hold its icon, or Settings > Apps > YouTube > XSide Settings. The box above the options says plainly when installing without XSide features helps (the app refuses to launch because it detects a change). Preflight warnings now show where Install is pressed.
  • The first-launch sheet explains before iOS asks. It now has pages: Installed with XSide, then Local network (why: refresh or pause from the iPhone, settings kept in step with the Mac; what happens if you refuse) and Notifications (the reminder before expiry), each shown only when iOS will ask, with its prompt right after it. Nothing reaches the network before the Local network page was read, whatever the XSide messages are set to; an app installed earlier shows that page on its own before its first network access. Apps that use the local network themselves (e.g. to cast) can make iOS ask before that page: once iOS has shown a question over the app, XSide checks silently first, and skips the page when the access is already allowed, or shows a short page saying it was refused and where to turn it back on. The page names the app ("YouTube talks to XSide on your Mac…").
  • New xside commands: xside apps and xside devices (--json too); xside settings <app> shows an app's XSide module settings, and xside settings <app> reminder=off level=essentials… changes them as Settings > My apps does (--device for one device); xside pause <app> [2h|30m|1d] and xside resume <app> for one app; xside uninstall <app> (asks first unless --yes); xside logs [-f]; xside report writes the logs archive and prints its path. Apps are named by name or bundle id, any case; when several match, xside lists them. xside waits for a long uninstall or report as long as it takes, saying it's still working; exit status 2 means the outcome isn't known yet (see the panel).
  • A "Build & contribute" page in Settings: make XSide yours (changes of your own with an AI agent, scripts with the xside command) and share it back if you want. Opens AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md on GitHub, copies a starter prompt for an agent, lists the real xside commands.
  • iPhone Duo compatibility, an install option per device (step 2 of the install window, the summary, and Settings > My apps): Add iPhone Duo compatibility lets an app built before SDK 27.1 use all of the iPhone Duo's screens, inner and outer, in Duo mode. XSide declares SDK 27.1 in the app's executable (with Xcode's vtool, keeping its minimum iOS) and its Info.plist, and, when the app has no scene manifest, adds one naming the app's own scene delegate, found in its executable. An app that has no scene support at all (no manifest, no scene delegate of its own) gets a small compatibility module of XSide's instead (independent of the XSide module), which adopts the app's window and passes it links, quick actions and the move to and from the background; the option then says so, with a stronger warning (the display and some behaviors may be imperfect), an app that starts from an old interface file (nib) gets a warning that it may show black, and the install step says the module was added; a crash in that module is named, with Reinstall without Duo compatibility. Highlighted on a Duo for an app not made for it (the preflight says so too), "not recommended" on other devices, greyed when the app already supports the Duo, and not available for an app without scene support when this build of XSide has no compatibility module; whatever its state, the option keeps its full explanation, with one highlighted line saying why it's recommended or not. Off unless turned on, after a confirmation (the app wasn't made for it: glitches are possible). Works with or without the XSide module, is kept across refreshes, and never fails an install: if it can't be added, the app is installed without it and the window and the panel say so; the install shows its own step, Adding iPhone Duo compatibility, with how it went. Sometimes just relaunching the app is enough for it to adapt.
  • iPhone Duo compatibility: action sheets in old apps. Like their alerts, the menus of choices old apps show (UIActionSheet, which iOS turns off for apps declaring a recent SDK) are shown again by the compatibility module, with the same buttons and answers to the app; on a wide screen they open as a popover pointing where the app asked.
  • iPhone Duo option: Learn more. Like the iCloud option, the Duo option has a Learn more popover (what it does, what can go wrong, how to undo, only on an iPhone Duo), and an app that already supports the Duo gets a neutral explanation instead of "it wasn't made for this".
  • Tweaks. Add tweaks to an app (.deb, .dylib, .framework or .bundle) and XSide injects them when it signs the app, without a jailbreak. They have their own step in the install window, ③ Tweaks (① Devices, ② Install, ③ Tweaks, ④ XSide module in the app), and are also added by dropping the file on an app's row in the panel, and managed later in Settings > My apps. Everything is per device, like the other options: each tweak has its own switch for each device, the summary lists the tweaks per device, and the panel shows each app's tweak count and a converted tweak badge. XSide keeps the tweaks per app and re-adds them at every refresh (the same copy, checked again each time); a tweak you remove goes at the app's next signing, and a stored tweak the last signing injected stays on. A tweak is added only to the 64-bit part of the app; when the app has no room left for another library the tweak is skipped, and the window and the panel say so. Update asks the trusted repo for a newer version only when you click.
  • Each tweak is checked and classified, with the reason. Compatible as is, converted (what XSide changes is listed) or not compatible (why: it needs a jailbreak, it works in SpringBoard or another system process that only a jailbroken device lets a tweak into, it was made for another app, it isn't built for the app's processor, it needs a newer iOS, a dependency is missing, nothing in it can be added to an app…). A tweak that isn't compatible isn't added, unless you choose Inject anyway (it then shows as Injected anyway). System tweaks need a jailbreak and can't be made to work.
  • Automatic conversion, with a warning. A tweak made for a jailbreak is converted so it can run in an app: its hooking library (Substrate, Substitute or libhooker) is replaced by ElleKit, added to the app; the jailbreak's folders it reads (/var/jb, /Library/...) are redirected to its own copy inside the app by a small library of XSide's (XSideTweakSupport); the common dependency Cephei is built into the app and libroot is built into the tweak (a Depends: libroot is satisfied). A converted tweak asks for one confirmation (the app may crash or the tweak may not behave correctly) and is marked as converted. Not converted: a tweak's settings page (it uses its defaults; a note says so).
  • What works and what doesn't, tested on an iPhone Duo (iOS 27.3). Hooks on Objective-C methods (MSHookMessageEx and the like) work, with the redirect of jailbreak paths and Cephei's preferences. Hooks on C functions (MSHookFunction, LHHookFunctions, substitute_hook_functions) don't: iOS kills the app when a tweak patches its code without a jailbreak. XSide warns on the tweak's card when it finds such hooks (only its Objective-C hooks work), and, if the app is killed that way, the crash diagnosis names the tweak and says why. Refreshing the app won't help; disable the tweak. Shell commands run by a tweak can't work either (no shell without a jailbreak). The classification, the conversion and the hooks were checked on that device only; other iOS versions and devices haven't been tested.
  • Dependencies, with where each comes from. When a tweak depends on other packages, XSide lists each with its status: provided by XSide (Cephei, libroot; ElleKit and the support library come with every converted tweak), added by you or missing. A missing one shows Where to find it (its official page, when XSide knows it) or a search (Canister, iOS Repo Updates) and Add its .deb…, which checks the package and its version. A dependency XSide knows no source for also offers Search the web. While a dependency is missing, the tweak can't be turned on; once added, it shows under the tweak (↳), turned on where it unblocks the tweak (from the kept copy when XSide already downloaded it, which the line says), and each device has its own status. An app loads only one copy of a dependency: XSide uses the one that suits every tweak on the device (yours first), finds a rootful copy's frameworks in usr/lib, and shows two tweaks that need versions no single copy satisfies as a conflict to settle. Not embedded: AltList (it needs Apple's private headers to build) and libGCUniversal (no licence found); a .deb you add always wins over XSide's copy.
  • Downloading a dependency, only from trusted sources, after you confirm. Download appears only for a dependency XSide knows a trusted source for, and you see what will be downloaded and from where before anything is. Over HTTPS only, from a list of repos shipped with XSide (never a setting): the Release file, the Packages index checked against its hashes, the .deb checked against the index's SHA256 and size; sizes and timeouts are capped, redirects stay on the repo's host, nothing is executed, everything is logged, and a refresh never downloads. Only a package with exactly the allowlisted id is accepted (not a Provides alias), and a kept copy is reused only while its repo is still trusted for that package. A second mechanism, the author's GitHub releases, exists for a dependency pinned to its author's repository (the .deb of a release, GitHub hosts only, size capped, the .deb's package and version checked; no published fingerprint, and the confirmation says so). Today the only trusted repo is Chariz (Cephei, which XSide already provides, and Alderis), and Alderis is the one dependency pinned to its author's GitHub releases (hbang/Alderis), asked only when Chariz fails or lacks the version, the newest release that has a .deb for the tweak's architecture. opa334's repo publishes no hashes and opa334/AltList has no GitHub releases, so AltList shows Where to find it and Add its .deb…, not Download.
  • Downloaded dependencies, in Settings > Tweaks. Every app's kept downloads on one page (package, version, repo, size, which app and tweak use it; My apps links to it). Uninstall… removes one from the devices and apps you check (grouped by device, everything checked at first): the tweaks there that need it are turned off, with Off: you removed … (not To settle), from each app's next refresh. XSide's own copy of a dependency is used unless it can't serve every tweak there; a downloaded copy only fills that gap (a .deb you added still wins), and goes away with the tweak that needed it, signed or not. A download nothing uses any more is deleted by itself (and logged): when its app, installation or device goes, or when its last tweak is removed; Used by shows real use only, and XSide never deletes one an installation still uses.
  • A tweak's description on its card. Step ③ and Settings > My apps > Tweaks show the .deb's description (written by its author, shown as is) in grey under the version and author: two lines, then Show more / Show less, the whole text on hover; Downloaded dependencies shows it on hover over the name. A .dylib or a .deb without one shows nothing. Tweaks added before get it from the download XSide kept, when it still has it; others get it once added again.
  • The tweaks of an app, listed on the iPhone. In iOS Settings, Tweaks · N opens a page with one group per tweak injected at the last signing, with its name (· converted when XSide converted it), its version and author, and its description (in its author's language, cut to about 300 characters). It sits inside the app's XSide Settings page, at the end; an app signed without XSide's features (no XSide page) keeps the row on the app's own page instead. Read-only: tweaks are still managed from XSide on the Mac. Nothing when the app has no tweak.
  • Tweaks in three groups. Step ③ and Settings > My apps sort the tweaks into To settle (a missing dependency, a dependency conflict, a tweak made for another app that isn't injected anyway: Next and Install wait until it's settled or removed, and Remove the tweaks to settle does it at once), Ready (what will be injected, a switch per device, see the changes for a converted one) and Not compatible (foldable, never injected). Every row has a trash and Remove in its context menu.
  • Crashes in a tweak, explained and fixed in one click. When an app crashes in a tweak XSide injected, the crash window and the panel name the tweak and offer Disable this tweak; when it crashes in what XSide added for converted tweaks (ElleKit, the support library, Cephei…), Disable the converted tweaks. Either fix applies to this device or to all devices that have the tweak, and the tweaks stay in XSide to turn back on. Only XSide's own copies count: an app's own ElleKit or library of the same name is never blamed on a tweak. A tweak that crashed running a shell command (impossible without a jailbreak) says so. Request a fix and Report a problem list the injected tweaks and what was converted.
  • Third-party code built from source, with its licences in About > Third-party licences. ElleKit (BSD-3-Clause, v1.1.3), Cephei (Apache-2.0, modified by XSide, with the changes stated as the licence requires) and zstd (BSD, a decompressor to read the .debs) are built from pinned sources in scripts/bundle.sh and scripts/release.sh refuses a build without their licences.
  • Simulate signed-out iCloud, an install option per device (step 2 of the install window, the summary, and Settings > My apps): With a free account XSide can give no app iCloud, and an app that uses it often crashes at its first iCloud call. With the option, XSide adds a small library of its own (independent of the XSide module) that makes the app believe no iCloud account is signed in instead of crashing: CloudKit (no account; every request fails "not authenticated", operations finish), Core Data and SwiftData with iCloud and CKSyncEngine (they wait for an account), settings synced through iCloud (kept on the device) and iCloud Drive (seen as unavailable). Data stays on the device, nothing syncs; an app that requires iCloud to work usually launches, but may stay on its sign-in screen. XSide reads the app's entitlements at import: when they declare iCloud, the option is highlighted and the preflight warns that the app may crash; an app that only links CloudKit (many do without using it) gets no warning, the option just says it's useful if the app crashes because of iCloud; for an app that doesn't use iCloud, it says it isn't needed. With a paid team, which keeps the app's iCloud, the option is no longer recommended (the preflight and the option say XSide keeps the app's iCloud, not yet tried with a real paid team) but stays available. Off unless turned on, after a confirmation (not from the crash fix button), kept across refreshes, its own install step (Adding signed-out iCloud); if it can't be added the app is installed without it and the window and the panel say so, and why when the app had room for only one more library (XSide's module keeps it; turning the XSide features off for the app makes room). When an app crashes in iCloud, the crash box, banner and window offer Reinstall with signed-out iCloud; a crash in the library itself is named, with Reinstall without signed-out iCloud. The library does nothing unless the app's Info.plist says XSide turned the option on, and XSide's libraries in an .ipa it signed before (signed-out iCloud, the XSide module, the Duo compatibility module) are removed with their load commands when their option is off. Like the Duo option, it always shows its full explanation, with a highlighted line for how it stands for the app.
  • A paid developer team keeps the app's iCloud. When the signing team is a paid one (Xcode says it isn't the free Personal Team), XSide no longer drops the app's iCloud: its containers, iCloud Drive and key-value store move to your team's identifiers (as its bundle id does), Xcode sets them up when it makes the profile, and the app is signed with what the profile grants. If Xcode refuses, the app is signed without iCloud as before. With a free account nothing changes. Not yet tried with a real paid team.
  • Compatibility fixes: the iPhone Duo and signed-out iCloud options have their own section, apart from the other install options, in step 2 of the install window, its summary and Settings > My apps ("XSide changes the app so it works better on your device or with a free account").
  • 32-bit code removal, shown with the compatibility fixes. Step 2, the summary and Settings > My apps always list 32-bit code removal (armv7), automatic, with whether it applies to the app (it has armv7/armv7s code, removed at signing, or only 64-bit code) and what it does.
  • What's in an IPA, before you install it. An IPA found on the internet may have been changed by anyone: at the top of the install window's first step (and of its summary), What's in this IPA lists what someone added to the original app (loose libraries, tweak frameworks such as CydiaSubstrate or ElleKit, libraries signed by another team), each with its name, place, size, how it's loaded and whether it's a tweak, a tweak library or unknown (no name or author), or says Nothing was added to the original app. Warning signs in those additions are shown in orange (an address account thieves use: Discord webhook, Telegram bot, paste site, ngrok and the like, a raw IP address; and, in an unknown addition or one with such an address, reading the keychain, watching the clipboard, reading every cookie, downloading code and running it), with the accesses the app can ask for (camera, microphone, location, local network, notifications…). Nothing blocks the install, and XSide says it can't guarantee an app is safe (Learn more opens the README's section). Settings > My apps shows the same in the app's ⋯ menu, IPA contents…, read from the IPA XSide kept (an app imported before is read again the first time). Read on the Mac only; nothing is sent anywhere.
  • Why an app crashes, in plain words. When XSide opens an app after installing it and the app doesn't stay open, XSide reads its newest crash report on the device and says why, in the install window and on its row in the panel: the app doesn't support iOS scenes (with what to do when the iPhone Duo option caused it), a library or a function is missing (named, the app's own or iOS's), a signature problem, a crash in the XSide module or in a tweak or library added to the app (named), iCloud (with a paid team, the diagnosis says XSide kept it), out of memory, too slow to start or not responding, or else the exception and where it happened. Each comes with what to do. On demand from an app's ... menu (Why does it crash?, the last 24 hours), with the technical details and a cleaned copy of the report (device, account and personal identifiers masked), and from the Terminal with xside crash <app> [--device <name>] [--json]. Report a problem includes the diagnosis and the cleaned reports. Only the few reports that may be the app's are copied from the device, into a temporary folder deleted right after reading; nothing is sent anywhere.
  • A crash you can't miss, seen almost at once. When XSide knows an app stopped, its row in the panel shows a red box under the row, across its width ("Stopped at launch: <cause>", or "Stopped while in use: <cause>") with See why and Ignore, and a red badge on its icon; a launch crash's box goes away by itself once the app is seen running again (the XSide module checks in, or it stays up after XSide opens it), a crash while in use's once the app has since been used and closed normally, and either once a reinstall is followed by a check that finds no new crash. The install window shows a red banner with the cause, See why, and the fix when XSide can apply it (Reinstall without XSide features, for that device only or, asked when the app is on several, for all of them; Reinstall without Duo compatibility, Reinstall without signed-out iCloud, Sign and reinstall); the crash window has the same button. Crashes that happen later are noticed within seconds or minutes: the XSide module keeps a small marker in the app's container and, at the next launch, tells XSide (in its signed check-in, once the local network is allowed) that the previous run stopped while in use; an app open on screen says goodbye on its live connection when it leaves, so a connection that drops without it means the app vanished; either way XSide reads that app's newest crash report at once. For every app, with or without the module, XSide lists each connected device's crash reports every 2 minutes, every 15 seconds for 3 minutes after an install, after XSide opens an app, or at an app's first check-in after 10 minutes without one (the check-ins that follow don't extend it), never while the device is being refreshed, and less often while the device can't answer (locked, out of reach); only the few new reports of its own apps are copied. A new crash posts a notification (once per crash report) that opens the crash window (macOS is asked for permission then if it never was, and every outcome is logged); the crash a fix answered never comes back as a new one; Settings > Notifications > Notify me when an app crashes and the device's own notification switch turn it off. Why does it crash? stays in the app's ... menu.
  • A crash for a missing permission text, named. When iOS stops an app for asking for private data (Apple Music, the camera, the photos…) without the text that explains why, the crash diagnosis names what it asked for; with iPhone Duo compatibility, which makes iOS require that text, it says XSide adds it at the next signing and offers Sign and reinstall, and otherwise asks you to report it.
  • Request a fix: the crash window's button opens a GitHub request titled with the app's name and filled with the diagnosis (cause, library, iOS and XSide versions, which fixes were on), cleaned of anything personal (no bundle or team id, no device name); Settings > Build & contribute has a card for a request of your own (a fix for one app, or for an iOS service like iCloud).
  • Pending signing-time changes, in one bar. Settings > My apps shows the app's detail in three tabs (XSide module, Fixes, Tweaks, each with a badge for what is pending or to settle; the tab you pick is kept from one app to the next), and one bar under the header: N pending changes, which ones (XSide features in this app, iPhone Duo compatibility, signed-out iCloud, tweaks), apply at the next refresh and Refresh now. Each pending option or tweak has a small pending badge, and an app with pending changes an orange dot in the list. Once a refresh of that app starts (from here, the panel, a notification or the schedule), the bar follows it: its step and progress, then Changes applied (a few seconds) or why it failed, with See details and Try again. The fixes' long explanations fold behind Learn more. Settings that sync live to the module (pill, reminder...) don't count.
  • A red dot on the menu-bar icon when something needs a look: an app stopped, a refresh failed (or an app expires soon without one), a tweak was left out at signing, signing no longer works, an app expired. Its description names each reason, and it goes once resolved.

Changed

  • The connection between the XSide module and the Mac is now encrypted. What an app tells XSide on the local network (its settings, version, last refresh, how its last run ended) and XSide's answers can no longer be read by someone on the same Wi-Fi, and the app is named by an opaque token instead of its identifiers. Keys come from the secret XSide writes into the app at each signing; every message is still signed and checked before it is read. Apps signed by an earlier XSide keep working as they are and switch over at their next refresh.
  • "XSide in the apps" is now "XSide module in the apps" (Settings page, install step 3, What's New).
  • Settings reorganized into General, Refreshing, Installing, XSide module in the apps (defaults for new installs), My apps, Tweaks, Notifications, Xcode and signing, Updates, Reports & Logs, Build & contribute, About.
  • Settings > My apps starts with the device (a segmented control, or a menu with more than three), then that device's apps, then the app's settings: each app on a device has its own settings. No more device tabs on the right.
  • Windows sized to what they show: each Settings page makes the window as tall as it needs (within the screen), so pages no longer scroll at the default text size; the install window gives its steps all the room the screen leaves.
  • The install window is wider, step 3 in two columns: the steps fit without scrolling (it still scrolls on a small screen).
  • The install progress matches what really happens: the module step shows as skipped (not ticked) for an app installed as is, the install step says when the app is deleted from the device first, and the list under the module step tells what is written into the app now and what the module does once the app opens.
  • The install window lists what Injecting the XSide module does from the start of the install, greyed until that step runs, then ticked.
  • The install step "Adding XSide features" is "Injecting the XSide module", and says "skipped (installed as is)" when it was.
  • Refresh now from the iPhone says what happens next: "refresh asked of your Mac, the app will close when it's done (about 1 min), open it again then", until the outcome (done, refused and why, or the Mac unreachable and what to do).
  • XSide Settings (touch and hold the icon, or a pill) opens the app's page in iOS Settings, where XSide's row is (iOS gives apps no way to open a page under theirs).
  • XSide's switches use the brand gradient and respond to the keyboard (focus ring, Space).
  • The Messages XSide and Language choices use XSide's own popup (brand chevron box) instead of the grey system one.
  • In the app, XSide's texts — pills, the first-launch sheet and the card — wrap and grow instead of being cut or touching the screen's edges (the sheet's "These details stay in Settings > ..." line, long pills), and a pill's button sits under its text. With every XSide message off, no pill shows on its own; the answers to a Refresh you asked for (and to a pill's button) still show.
  • The answer to a Refresh asked from the iPhone that arrives while you're in another app shows when you come back (within 10 minutes). "XSide on your Mac doesn't know this app" also suggests checking the date and time.
  • Settings > My apps says when an app was installed by an earlier XSide (reachable after its next refresh), and an app whose XSide module couldn't be added counts as installed without XSide features.
  • XSide's Bonjour service is published as "XSide" rather than under the Mac's name.
  • Resuming an app's refreshes from the panel keeps the panel open; after a row's confirmation (stop refreshing, uninstall, remove from the list) the panel opens again.
  • While every refresh is paused from the panel, each app row looks paused too ("all refreshes paused"), and comes back on resume.
  • Settings > Build & contribute installs the xside command right from its terminal card (or says where it is), as General does.
  • Existing apps get their per-app values from today's global settings (the global reminder switch becomes each app's reminder; the others start on).
  • The panel's footer: Export logs is gone (Report a bug brings the logs) and About is the last button. The panel's hover bubbles keep their width and stay inside the panel.
  • Step ④ and My apps: an app this device already connected (local network allowed) says Already connected · reconnects as soon as you reopen the app after a reinstall, instead of Not connected yet.
  • The panel's app rows no longer show a refresh button on hover: Refresh now is in the row's ... menu (and its right-click menu).
  • The app's SDK is read from its executable at import. The "built for an older iOS" preflight note no longer shows: outside an iPhone Duo the layout difference it promised mostly isn't there, and on a Duo the iPhone Duo note says what matters (and only offers the option when the app can take it).

Fixed

  • A device Xcode can't see is said as such. When xcodebuild can't find the device (unplugged, locked, or its connection down: « Unable to find a destination matching the provided destination specifier » and its variants), XSide no longer says it couldn't create a provisioning profile: it names the device and tells you to plug it in or unlock it, then try again.

item.title: XSide 1.0.6-beta
item.description:
Added

  • Notifications per device (the device's … menu in the panel): turn them off for an iPhone you manage for someone else; its apps are still refreshed, without any notification on this Mac (the reminder the app shows on the phone itself stays).
  • xside pause [2h|30m|1d] and xside resume pause and resume automatic refreshes from the Terminal; xside status says while they're paused.
  • Updates can be checked every hour; XSide also checks when it starts and after each app refresh (at most every 10 minutes).
  • The install window warns when an app wasn't built for the device's iOS (it may open in compatibility mode, e.g. a YouTube built with the iOS 26 SDK on an iOS 27 iPhone), and when it's older than the version already installed.
  • Each app in the panel shows its installed version.
  • Installing another version of an app over the one on the device: its card says "Updated by XSide" (or "Older version installed by XSide"), with the new and the previous version, instead of "Refreshed by XSide".

Changed

  • The XSide sheet in apps follows the reader's text size (Dynamic Type) and scrolls when it doesn't fit (landscape, large text).
  • "Last refreshed" in the app's iOS Settings section is the time it was signed, not the profile's creation.

Fixed

  • xside pause refuses a duration past a year instead of crashing on a huge number, and a garbled pause request is refused instead of pausing until resumed.
  • xside status counts the next refresh with the chosen days before expiry (it assumed 2), says when refreshes are paused, and --json has pausedUntil.
  • Version checks read the leading digits of each part ("1.10a" is newer than "1.9", "21.37.04" equals "21.37.4"), and the "older version" warning only compares the same copy of an app.
  • An update found again after "Remind me later" no longer notifies more than once a day.

item.title: XSide 1.0.5-beta
item.description:
Added

  • XSide in your apps. Every app XSide installs says where it comes from and until when it works: after an install, a sheet with the XSide logo, the expiry date and the days left (in its own window, so the app's screens can't cover or close it); after a refresh, a smaller card at the bottom, closed with OK. A new install step, "Adding XSide features", lists what's added.
  • A reminder on the device, the day before an app expires, with XSide's logo, sent by the app itself. If the app never asked for notifications, the permission is asked once, when the install sheet is closed, and the sheet says why beforehand.
  • An "Installed with XSide" section in the app's iOS Settings page (Settings > Apps > the app): valid until, last refreshed, and XSide's address. Rewritten at each refresh; the app's own settings stay as they were. The install sheet says where to find it.
  • The app opens on the device after an install, which also tells whether the device trusts the developer. If not, XSide opens Settings > General > VPN & Device Management on the device itself, and the guide says so (with a button to open it again). If it does, no guide. When the device can't tell (locked), the guide shows on a first install, after the last XSide app was deleted from the device, or with a new certificate.
  • Apps deleted from the device stay deleted. XSide notices (before a refresh, every 10 minutes on each reachable device, and when the panel opens), removes them from its list, drops their reminder, and says so in a notification. A refresh no longer puts them back.
  • Choose when apps refresh (Settings > General > Automatic refreshes): 1, 2 (default) or 3 days before they expire; pause (1 hour, until tomorrow morning, until resumed), also from a new Pause tile in the panel, which says while refreshes are paused; only on power adapter; a preferred time (night or evening). An app expiring within 12 hours is refreshed anyway, and refreshes you start yourself are never held back.
  • Report a problem (Settings > Reports & Logs, and the bug button in the panel): opens XSide's bug form on GitHub, filled in with the versions, the devices, XSide's state and the last log lines, and saves the full log archive on the Desktop to drag into it. The issue doesn't name your apps (<app-1>…); device names, serial numbers, account and team are masked in both, and nothing is sent until you submit.
  • Settings > General > Installs and devices: open the app after an install and open the Trust page (both defaults, changeable in each install's Options), notice deleted apps, refresh new devices over Wi-Fi or not. Settings > Notifications: the reminder on the device, the notification when a deleted app leaves the list.
  • The install window's device tiles say what stops an install there: "Developer Mode off", or "Unlock it" after an attempt failed on a locked device.

Changed

  • The trust guide shows a single step without a number, and no longer starts with "Then".
  • The shared keychain option says to turn it on when signing in fails ("can't sign in", "app not verified").
  • Settings > Logs is now Reports & Logs, with Report a problem first.

Fixed

  • Reminders in tweaked apps that pretend to be another app (e.g. a modded YouTube reporting "com.google.ios.youtube" for Google sign-in): iOS refused them notifications without asking. XSide now asks with the app's real identity, and an app name with special characters ("YouTube +") gets a plain internal name.
  • A device with Developer Mode off: the install window says so and how to turn it on, and doesn't start an install that can only fail. If it fails anyway, the message says Developer Mode is off instead of "Couldn't create the provisioning profile".
  • A locked device that Xcode has to prepare for development: the message says to unlock it, instead of "Couldn't create the provisioning profile".
  • A device out of reach during an uninstall (CoreDevice error 1011) is reported as unreachable, not as a failed uninstall.

item.title: XSide 1.0.4-beta
item.description:
Added

  • Command line tool xside: status, refresh <app>, refresh --all, install <file.ipa>, open. Installed from Settings > General; starts XSide in the background when it isn't running.
  • Update notifications: a new version found in the background shows a notification and a banner in the panel, instead of a window that could open behind others.
  • Install updates automatically (Settings > Updates): downloaded in the background and installed as soon as nothing runs; XSide relaunches itself, then says "XSide x.y was installed".
  • Sparkle's update window shows the version's changelog.

Fixed

  • When Xcode drops its Apple Account (a known Xcode bug), one notification instead of one each time it flickers back; the message says what happened.
  • "Open Xcode" says to press ⌘ + comma or use the Xcode > Settings… menu (its Settings then open on Apple Accounts), since Xcode can't be opened straight on them.
  • A beta Xcode counts as ready only once its license is accepted, and isn't checked again at every probe.
  • The panel's footer buttons show their hover color and label again.
  • The quit confirmation no longer holds up an update relaunching XSide.
  • Sparkle's "Version History" opens the page of all releases.
